_comment: Production alert rules for the Grafana Cloud stack (IFC-032). Applied by tools/scripts/grafana/apply-alert-rules.mjs through the Grafana provisioning API (workflow: grafana-alert-rules.yml). Metrics are the span metrics Grafana Cloud generates from our OTLP traces: traces_spanmetrics_calls_total{service, span_name, span_kind, status_code} and the traces_spanmetrics_latency histogram (seconds). A rule with its own datasourceUid queries that datasource instead: grafanacloud-logs is Loki (LogQL over our OTLP logs, labelled service_name). Routed by the default notification policy to the owner's email contact point.

rules.title: Production telemetry stopped (ai-worker sends no spans)
rules.replaces: ifc032-otel-collector-down (there is no collector; the hosted gateway receives directly)
rules.why: Covers the combined worker (service intelliflow-ai-worker) as well as ai-worker. The rate is summed across both names, so while either still sends spans the rule stays quiet; a cutover from one to the other cannot raise a false 'silent'.
rules.summary: Neither ai-worker nor the combined worker (intelliflow-ai-worker) has sent spans for 15 minutes. Either the worker is down (as ai-worker was from June to October 2026) or OTLP export broke.

rules.title: Lead routing failures
rules.summary: More than 5 lead-routing workflow spans ended in error in 5 minutes.

rules.title: Workflow error rate above 1%
rules.summary: More than 1% of workflow spans ended in error over 5 minutes.

rules.title: Lead routing p95 latency above 500 ms
rules.summary: p95 duration of workflow.lead.route spans is above 500 ms.

rules.title: API server error rate above 5%
rules.summary: More than 5% of api server spans ended in error over 10 minutes.

rules.title: Error spans in ai-worker or api (direct, fast detection)
rules.why: IFC-074 MTTD: Grafana Asserts' ErrorRatioBreach fires 180-360 s after the first error. The first version of this rule (2m window, evaluated at now) never fired in 24 h of production (24-25 Oct 2026): span metrics land 60-120 s after the error and reach the ruler more than 60 s later, when a 2m increase is already back to 0. A 5m window read 60 s back fires on every replayed episode across 60-120 s of ingest lag, at a modelled mean of 162-203 s.
rules.summary: ai-worker, the combined worker or api recorded error spans in the 5 minutes up to 1 minute ago.

rules.title: Error-level logs in ai-worker (direct, fast detection)
rules.why: IFC-074 MTTD < 120 s. No span-metrics rule can get there: the first sample lands 60-120 s after the error and reaches the ruler more than 60 s later. Loki ingests a log line in seconds. Replayed on run 7 (24-25 Oct 2026, 13 error episodes): every episode that wrote an error-level line (9 of 13) fires, at a modelled mean of 36-61 s for 5-30 s of ingest lag; all 9 two-minute buckets with error lines fell on a real episode (0 false alarms). The other 4 wrote no error-level line and stay with the span rules. Only ai-worker ships logs to Loki: the combined worker logs as ai-worker and the api ships none, so api errors are left to the span rules. 'Latency alert generated' is excluded: it is the worker's own latency monitor, logged at warn, which older images tagged severity=critical (55 an hour on 28 Oct 2026).
rules.expr: sum by (service_name) (count_over_time({service_name="ai-worker"} != "Latency alert generated" | detected_level=~"(?i)error|fatal|critical" or severity_text=~"(?i)error|fatal|critical" [2m]))
rules.summary: ai-worker (the combined worker) logged error-level lines in the last 2 minutes.

deliveryTest.title: IFC-032 delivery test (expected; deleted on the next normal run)
deliveryTest.summary: Test alert proving that production alerts reach the owner's email. Safe to ignore.
